validates: our CALL of the frozen scorer: column choice, pair orientation, and the two-order arithmetic in _score_pair
does_not_validate: generalisation - the checkpoint was fitted on this dataset, so this is in-sample while the paper's 0.845 is 10-fold cross-validated
the study's own distribution - we score model rewrites of human texts, not this dataset's human/LLM paraphrase pairs

annotator_agreement.note: pairwise = how well two annotators agree. mean_label_reliability = Spearman-Brown of that to the 3-rater mean, which is the actual target. attainable_ceiling = its square root: the highest correlation ANY predictor could have with labels this noisy. Compare 0.845 against the ceiling, not 1.

verdict: wiring confirmed by the training-free length baseline
in_sample_note: rho(scorer, human) = 0.964 is IN-SAMPLE and is NOT comparable with the paper's held-out 0.845; the gap is the expected train/test difference, not a better result.
